reviewer: current assistant visual inspection; not human or physical-camera calibration
visual_consistency_findings: Left-wrist camera retains its own nearby finger and an oblique scene view while the inactive left arm remains stationary.
Right-wrist view changes substantially during approach; the bottle becomes large and remains near the visible right fingertips during physical holding.
Head, left and right images contain distinct viewpoints consistent with the source mapping; no obvious swapped or duplicated views are observed.
The cylindrical bottle looks horizontal in the wrist images because of their optical-frame roll and perspective; measured world upright angle remains 0 degrees in the final trace.
limitations: The head view puts the small bottle near the lower edge and cuts off part of the body at several stages.
Nominal wrist mounts are simulation presets rather than measured physical D435 extrinsics.
Source-bound mapping plus saved-image consistency is not a direct runtime extrinsic readback or a proof of optimal camera placement.
Images show the minimum one-bottle collection scene, not the earlier full tabletop presentation scene.
